desc: Implement the complete generateString solution: T-placement with conflict detection, 'a'-fill, prevFree precomputation, and left-to-right F-window fixing at the rightmost free position
Verify the greedy invariant (a fix at the rightmost free position never un-breaks an earlier F window) and confirm O(n*m) complexity fits n<=1e4, m<=500

Test against the three provided examples plus edge cases: str1="F"/str2="a" (expect "b"), all-T with periodic str2, fully-forced matching F-window (expect ""), overlapping F windows sharing a free position
**T-overlay with conflict detection** — correct; overlapping T-windows demanding different chars at a shared cell yield `""` (Example 2 confirmed: conflict at index 2).

**Fix logic soundness** — when window `i` matches str2 and `p` is its rightmost free cell, `word[p]` must equal `str2[p-i]`, and since free cells only ever hold `'a'`/`'b'`, the flip (`'b'` if `str2[p-i]=='a'` else `'a'`) always breaks the match. The apparently dangerous `else 'a'` branch is safe because a matching window with `str2[p-i] != 'a'` implies a prior fix set `word[p]='b'`.

**No re-check invariant** — I attempted to construct a counterexample where fixing window `i` at `p` re-matches an earlier window `j` (requires `str2[p-j]='a'`, `str2[p-i]='b'`, plus periodicity `str2[k]=str2[k-d]` on the overlap). Every construction attempt (e.g., `str2="ba"`, `str2="bba"`) forces a T-placement that would cover `p`, contradicting `p` being free — confirming the worker's infinite-regress argument.

**Lexicographic optimality** — any valid solution must alter some free cell in each matching F-window; altering the rightmost one with the smallest possible char is optimal by the standard exchange argument, and the invariant guarantees fixes never need revisiting.
**Examples & edge cases** — all three provided examples plus `("F","a")→"b"` trace correctly; complexity `O(n·m) ≤ 5·10⁶` with `O(n+m)` space is well within limits.
